description:
Two substances, each filed as two rows, for the two ways a ceiling COMPARISON can go wrong that drug-reference-substance-dosing-ceilings.json cannot reach. Neither pair carries an ATC code, so no relevance gate can inject the second row for a reason other than the question naming the substance, and every band spans 0-120 so a patient's age never silences one.

Tinidazole 2000 / 500 is the ORDER pair: its ceilings disagree under numeric and lexicographic comparison, where every multi-row pair in that other file (3000/2000, 300/150, 4000/300, 4000/2000, 50/25, 60/30, 100/200) sorts identically either way, so a sort of the ceiling SPELLINGS passes every case built on it while a sort of the NUMBERS is what production has to do. Here "2000" sorts before "500" as text and 500 before 2000 as a number. It matters because DosingCeilingFidelityCheck reads position 0 as the strictest and returns as soon as the answer states it: with the list reversed, an answer quoting the LAXER ceiling finds it at position 0, the walk goes silent, and the check stops seeing exactly the defect issue #276 reports — with nothing else in the suite going red. The two rows publish the same mg/kg band, so their dosing NUMBERS differ only in the ceiling; their names differ too, as these fixtures' row pairs conventionally do — nothing requires it, and the sibling file's Ranitidine pair is deliberately two rows of one substance under ONE display name.

Levothyroxine 5 / 0.5 is the DECIMAL pair, and it exists because the ceilings are the first NUMERIC needles this module scans an answer for. DrugReference.formatNumber emits Double.toString for a non-integral value, so this substance publishes "5 mg/day" and "0.5 mg/day" — and the laxer one's spelling is a SUFFIX of a decimal a clinical answer can easily contain. ChartSearchAiUtils.statesWord bounds a needle on letters and digits alone, so it reads "2.5 mg/day" as stating "5 mg/day": a decimal point is neither. That is a false POSITIVE on a published key, the one direction this check must never fail in, which is why the ceilings are scanned with statesMeasurement instead. A pair whose ceilings are both integral cannot show it, and no other fixture here has a non-integral ceiling at all. Its two rows also differ in mg/kg, where the order pair's agree — so the two pairs are not two copies of one arrangement, and a change that collapsed the other-rows item to its ceiling alone would still leave this pair saying something the other does not.

Phenobarbital 600 / 200 / 60 is the THREE-ROW substance, and it is here because every other pair in this file and in the sibling one has exactly two rows — which makes the walk's central rule degenerate. DosingCeilingFidelityCheck reports the FIRST ceiling the answer states scanning UP from the strictest, so on a two-ceiling record the reported one is always the only candidate and a mutation reporting the LAST stated ceiling instead passes every case. With three, an answer stating 200 and 600 but not 60 must be reported as (stated 200, unstated 60) and not (stated 600, unstated 60): the smallest gap, which is the one a clinician needs. Its three ceilings also disagree between numeric and lexicographic order more thoroughly than the Tinidazole pair does — as text they sort 200, 60, 600 — the space in "60 mg/day" orders below the '0' of "600", which is the kind of thing a hand-derived sequence gets wrong, so this one is what `LC_ALL=C sort` and Java's own String comparator both return — and a spelling sort therefore puts a MIDDLE ceiling at position 0 rather than merely swapping two. The rows share one mg/kg band, so the ceiling is the only number that varies between them, and no row carries an ATC code.
